decisions.reason: A same-message INTRODUCE already captures the distinct endpoint-elevation decision, including the subtle reach increase, preserved geometry, and application across all three forms.

The selected terminal treatment does not replace the approved Hero V architecture; the source explicitly keeps that architecture locked, while the separate endpoint-elevation Requirement owns the narrowly requested reach adjustment.

The É accent remains literally derived from the Hero V terminal and retains its alignment and revision rules. Applying the shared terminal refinement consistently does not change those derivation semantics.
The source limits work to the shared terminals of the Hero V, second V, and É accent and explicitly keeps everything else unchanged; the internal E and L letterform rules are unaffected.

The second V retains its supporting role, optical construction, hierarchy, and alphabet relationship. Its participation in the shared reach adjustment is already owned by the dedicated endpoint-elevation Requirement rather than changing the second-V form rules.
The source changes terminal geometry while keeping the Satin finish and overall treatment framework unchanged; it makes no new material-finish or champagne-gold decision.
The source explicitly locks the overall architecture and changes only terminal nuances. Kerning, baseline, scale, case treatment, and composition rhythm remain unchanged.
Confidence, restraint, and architectural character are reasons for selecting Option B, not changes to the existing brand-expression requirements.
The terminal refinement does not alter the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
The source contains no change to the production-ready artwork deliverable or final asset-package requirements.
